notes:
Top-level: large European edge provider, heavy regulatory/commercial sensitivity around where logs and request traces live. Primary ask: private VPC deployment with strong network controls and integration to their KMS + SIEM. Short bullets below are excerpts from calls and internal notes.

- Company wants single-tenant VPC (private) in eu-west-1. No egress of request payloads to public internet except to specific monitoring endpoints.
- Prefer PrivateLink-style private endpoints but open to VPC peering if team provides CIDR plan; SecOps prefers PrivateLink due to tighter routing controls.
- Key asks: static IP allowlist for outbound egress to customer on-prem systems, IP ranges for Redwood ingress endpoints, port ranges 443 (mutual TLS) + 8443 for management plane, deny all other inbound.
- Egress controls: NAT + egress-only gateway policy; allowlist only to S3 endpoints for artifact storage and to their Splunk ingest IPs. No direct internet to third-party LLM repositories.
- KMS: must support AWS KMS key policies and optional HSM import; require envelope encryption for cache blobs and at-rest model artifacts.
- Audit logging: full request/response metadata (metadata only; not storing PII) to be mirrored to their Splunk instance and retained for 1 year; Redwood must support push to S3 + SNS for audit ingestion.
- Data residency: EU-only processing and storage; contractual clause requested.
- Compliance: SOC2 type II in place is a prerequisite; they will require a security FAQ and SOC2 report upload to their portal.
- Quote from CTO on call: "We cannot have an uncontrolled egress path — all model calls must be inside our VPC and logs forwarded to our SIEM."
- Pricing sensitivity: enterprise budget but strong desire to optimize token/unit costs — interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization.

technical_requirements: Private VPC deployment in eu-west-1 with dedicated subnets for runtime and control plane
Support for AWS PrivateLink endpoints and alternative VPC peering via Transit Gateway
Static egress IP allowlist for outbound connections to customer-managed SIEM and artifact storage
Mutual TLS (mTLS) for control plane connections; certificate exchange process required
KMS integration: customer-managed keys (AWS KMS), envelope encryption for caches and persisted artifacts
Audit log shipping: push events to customer S3 + Splunk HEC; logs must not contain raw PII payloads unless redaction enabled
Network hardening: deny-by-default firewall rules, explicit port rules (443/8443), route table controls, no public IPs on runtime nodes
Egress policy: NAT gateway or egress-only gateway with strict allowlist; no arbitrary outbound to public endpoints
network_security_requirements: Prefer PrivateLink over VPC peering — security team: PrivateLink lowers blast radius and simplifies routing
If peering used, require non-overlapping CIDR blocks and Transit Gateway to centralize routes
Firewall rules: inbound only from specified Redwood management IPs; outbound allowlist to customer IPs and cloud provider service endpoints
IP allowlists: need list of Redwood egress/ingress CIDRs (requested) and static IPs for SIEM/backup endpoints
TLS: TLS1.2+ with client certificates; optional mutual TLS for admin APIs
Route propagation: no dynamic route backdoors; explicit route table entries only; prefer AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints
Peering fallback: VPN fallback path for initial POC testing if PrivateLink setup takes longer
quotes_from_call: CTO: 'We cannot have an uncontrolled egress path — all model calls must be inside our VPC and logs forwarded to our SIEM.'
SecOps lead: 'PrivateLink gives us the simplest security justification to auditors; show us architecture and we can sign off.'

Success criteria: all inbound/outbound connections use approved paths; logs delivered to Splunk within 2 minutes; no traffic leaves eu-west-1
